target_paper.title: OffsetBias: Leveraging Debiased Data for Tuning Evaluators
target_paper.original_source: paper Table 4 (= appendix Table 6), row GPT-4o-0513, n=160

generation.substitute_snapshot: none - gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is the snapshot the paper itself judged with (config/gpt-4o.yaml, Sec. 5.3)
generation.parameters: system + user message from prompt/llmbar.py via module.InferenceModule.make_conversation; temperature 0; max_tokens 20; no top_p and no seed (config/gpt-4o.yaml); endpoint POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (harness/openai_client.py, raw HTTPS)
generation.battery: EvalBiasBench 160 samples (80 pairs x 2 orders) x 3 complete seeds = 480 archived calls in runs\W4404781910\baseline_alive/calls.jsonl; scored by the repository's own run_bench.add_parse_result / get_model_statistics; median over seeds; 95% CI = pair-level bootstrap (10000 resamples, rng 0)

total.orig_positional_agreement: not reported for EvalBiasBench (Table 2 covers LLMBar / HHH / MT-Bench)

bootstrap.unit: pair (80 pairs, both orders resampled together)

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 as the card instantiates it: survived = median total (3 seeds) inside the binomial band around the original 86.9 over 80 pairs AND far above chance AND at or above OffsetBias-8B 85.0; partial = outside the band but clearly above chance and above the 8B baselines; dead = at or near chance, or the ordering against OffsetBias-8B inverts by more than the CI. The six cells are secondary evidence. Human double-coding pending
results.note: total 88.8 vs paper 86.9 (delta +1.9), 95% CI [82.3, 94.0] over the 80 pairs; original binomial band [79.51, 94.29]; comparators OffsetBias-8B 85.0, GPT-3.5-0613 45.0, chance 50.0; positional agreement 92.5. Empty-reference cell 61.5 (paper 50.0): still at chance level, the paper qualitative point holds. median inside the original band [79.51, 94.29] and at or above OffsetBias-8B (85.0), far above chance

reproducibility_frictions_observed: item-level original judge outputs were never released (only Table 4 percentages at one decimal), so agreement with the 2024 run can be compared only at the accuracy level; the original per-cell counts used here are reconstructed from the printed percentages, each of which has a unique integer pre-image

module.py imports torch, transformers, vllm, fastchat and openai at module level although the OpenAI / biasbench path uses none of them; vllm and fastchat are not installable on this machine, so the adapter stubs them to reach InferenceModule's renderer and parser

run_bench.py opens its JSON files with the platform default encoding; on this Windows locale (cp949) the repository's own data loader raises UnicodeDecodeError, so text mode is forced to UTF-8 around the repository's calls
requirements.txt is unpinned (the openai SDK version of the original run is unknown); the re-run posts the same chat-completions body over raw HTTPS and logs the served model and system fingerprint
biasbench rows bypass run_bench.make_data_row, so they carry no id and are not stripped: item identity is positional (subset + index)

the card's protocol.messages paraphrase quotes '[Output (a)]'; the repository template asks for '"Output (a)"' and the parser regex requires 'Output (a)' at the start of a line, so a bracketed reply is label 4 = incorrect
the empty-reference cell rests on 13 pairs, so one flipped pair moves it by 7.7 pp (observed 61.5 vs 50.0, CI [37.2, 82.1]); it is not judged on its own
temperature 0 over the API is not deterministic; 3 complete seeds were run and the median is judged (per-seed totals [88.8, 88.8, 88.1])
